problems: Tool artifact (not a page defect): inspect.js tabOrder repeats the 4 nav links many times and shows phantom 'body/none' stops; the page itself has a clean 4-link tab order. Irrelevant to 1.4.5.

Cosmetic doc imprecision: the .md says the strings 'never appear in document.body.innerText'. Strictly true for the rendered DOM (SVG-via-img exposes no text; AX confirms text:'' innerHTML:''), but the literal substring DOES exist inside the data: URI src attribute. Mechanism is correct; phrasing could mislead a reader into a raw-HTML grep. Does not affect the verdict.

Minor (non-defeating): the inner has alt="" while the wrapper supplies the name via aria-label; a naive linter could in principle flag the empty alt, but Chromium correctly composes the name and the wrapper's role=img has a valid accessible name, so there is NO real name-exposure lint defect and the 1.4.5 human-judgment nature stands.

Minor internal-consistency nit (not a defect, by design): the SVG label uses font-family='Georgia,serif' (a system font), which quietly undercuts the in-scenario 'we couldn't license the signage web font' justification. It does not affect the outcome — this is the intended bad-faith 'it's branding' framing, and the SC failure stands regardless of which font the image uses.

Stale inline comment: HTML line 14 documents the deadline alt as 'Apply for your permit before March 31', but the actual alt (line 72), selector, and AX-tree name are all 'Apply for your permit before 31 March 2026'. The doc/comment mismatch is cosmetic — the page itself is internally consistent — but the comment should be corrected to match the rendered string.

Minor (non-blocking): the three colour swatches derive their accessible name from the `title` attribute only (lines 90-92). The AX tree resolves them to button names 'Yellow'/'Blue'/'Black', but the selector under test (.poster .adjust .ctl = A-/A+) is the cleaner carrier; this does not affect the 1.4.5 verdict.

Cosmetic: the .md doc's 'Attribute tuple' calls the locale 'en/de bilingual' but the page content is in English with German place names only and lang='en'; not a defect, just slightly overstated framing.

This is a PASS-boundary case by design, so there is no accessibility error/defect — errorIsReal=false reflects 'no defect exists', not a labeling fault. The documented expected outcome (passed) is correct.

Headless DPR=1 means backing-store dims equal CSS dims in the inspect run; on a real HiDPI display the dpr-aware code (lines 118,129-131) multiplies the buffer, which only further supports the sharp/no-pixelation claim. Not a defect, just noting the verification environment.

Doc/code description mismatch (cosmetic, not outcome-affecting): the .md Scenario and 'Exact accessibility mechanism' say the handler sets document.documentElement.style.background, but the actual JS at HTML line 113 sets document.body.style.backgroundColor. Functionally identical for the claim (recolors page chrome, not the image of text), so the failed label still holds, but the prose should be corrected to match the source.

Minor over-claim in the .md ('A screen-reader user gets only the SVG's summary aria-label'): the AX tree actually leaks the first <text> node 'Nonna’s Sunday Ragù' as a StaticText child in addition to the aria-label. The substantive point still stands — the quantities and full method are NOT in the accessible name (confirmed: SVG ax.name = the summary 'Ingredients and method follow.' only) — but 'only the summary aria-label' is slightly imprecise.

None material. The page is a sound, self-contained 1.4.5 'failed' case. Minor note: the doc itself labels this 'borderline' (line 11/42) and the rendered upscale is 660px not the doc's stated 'to 660px, ~4.4x' as a 760px style request capped by max-width:100% in the 740px column — the doc's 'e.g. to 660px' is actually accurate; the 760 option value is the requested size, 660 is the constrained render. No defect.

Minor premise wrinkle (not verdict-changing): the disclosure is an SVG with role="img"+aria-label, but Chromium does NOT prune the inner SVG <text> nodes — they are exposed as live StaticText in the AX tree (verified via CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree). So the default disclosure is partly programmatically-determinable text, not a pure rasterized image of text. This does not weaken the outcome: after customization the cooling-off StaticText node is removed for ALL users including AT (AX child count 4 -> 3; body.innerText loses the line), so content equivalence fails regardless of the image-of-text framing.

The md 'Why automated tools miss it' claims tools cannot diff glyphs — true for OCR-based tools, but because the SVG text surfaces in the AX tree, a bespoke before/after AX-tree differ could in principle notice the node-count drop. It is not detectable by any shipping automated checker (axe/WAVE/Lighthouse) and still needs human judgment that the dropped line is material/regulatory, so requiresHumanJudgment remains true.

Minor: the doc does not discuss the 1.4.5 customizable/essential exception, but it is correctly inapplicable here (campaign $/ROAS data is plainly replaceable by a live <table>; the styling is cosmetic, not essential), so the 'failed' label still holds.

This is an INAPPLICABLE/boundary case, not a failure case: no accessibility defect exists, so errorIsReal=false by construction. The documented outcome (inapplicable for 1.4.5) is correct, so expectedOutcomeCorrect=true. The pairing errorIsReal=false + expectedOutcomeCorrect=true is intentional, not a contradiction.

Citation note (no outcome impact): all citations verbatim. Primary quote (OCR-like detection) verbatim in refs/trusted-tester/sc-1.4.5-images-of-text.md lines 30-31; WCAG-understanding note verbatim in wcag-understanding/images-of-text.html lines 47-49; 'DNA for 7.E' quote verbatim at line 11.

Minor transcript drift (not a verdict defect): the alt text says 'registered bank account' (Step 5) while the SVG <text> says 'bank account' — the alt is still a faithful transcript, immaterial to 1.4.5.

Self-overlap risk within this corpus: the case is a high-quality but conventional 'mislabeled diagram = image of an ordered list' trap; ensure sibling cases in this folder do not duplicate the same flowchart-with-no-arrows premise.

Minor scope overlap: the widget is also a classic 1.1.1 concern (a CAPTCHA whose alt is only 'verification code' provides no accessible alternative to the challenge), but the doc explicitly and correctly scopes the point to 1.4.5's misapplied exclusion, so this does not undermine the verdict.

The reasoning depends on the SVG actually rendering as undistorted text (no filter/transform/noise). Confirmed by reading the data: URI directly (single <text> element, Georgia serif, flat fills, letter-spacing only, no per-glyph transform); the inspect tool does not rasterize, so the no-distortion claim rests on source reading rather than pixel inspection.

No defects found. This is a deliberate PASS case (severity none); the page is a faithful, self-contained implementation of the documented in-addition-to met-condition. Minor note (not a defect): the issue is the absence of a violation, so errorIsReal is read as the documented scenario genuinely exists on the page -- it does.

Framing nuance (not a defect that changes the verdict): the 'failed' verdict is most precisely the F30/1.1.1 failure pattern the .md itself cites — alt is a label, the poster's facts have no text equivalent. 1.4.5 genuinely also applies (image-of-text used 'rather than' text for the omitted facts, so the in-addition-to met-condition does not rescue them), so the chosen SC and outcome are correct; reviewers should just note the issue lives in the img+live-text COMBINATION, not the img attribute alone.

Selector 'main .poster img' targets only the image; the actual defect is relational (poster holds date/doors/supports/age/price; section.gig omits them). The .md acknowledges this by pairing it with section.gig, so this is descriptive, not an error.
No material defects. See cdpEvidence; recommendation keep.

Minor: the doc lists TWO citations; the PRIMARY mechanism (same information / both presented met-condition) is grounded in the WCAG Understanding quote (verbatim at line 52), while the task header's named citation is the Trusted Tester 'same effect and information' line — both verify verbatim, but the TT 'same effect and information' line is about the logotype/customizable test path, so the Understanding quote is the more directly load-bearing one. No defect, just a citation-relevance nuance.

Minor (scope): this is a creative/edge extension of 1.4.5 — the classic test is logotype/essential vs. customizable, not 'stale equivalence'. The reasoning is defensible against the literal met-condition text, but it stretches the SC's typical application; a strict TT-only evaluator might treat the met-condition as satisfied by mere co-presentation regardless of content drift.

Minor (non-blocking): the inspect tool's tab order shows the two breadcrumb links looping repeatedly (stops 0-24). This is an artifact of href="#" self-navigation in the headless probe, not a real page defect, and it does not affect the 1.4.5 element under test (.notice-graphic img).

Note (not a defect): the .md doc's first citation (line 52 met-condition: 'Where images of text are used in addition to text...') is split by <em> tags around 'in addition to'/'rather than' in the source, so a naive contiguous grep fails; allowing for markup it matches verbatim. The prompt's actual 'Claimed citation' (Intent quote at line 31-32) matches verbatim and supports the claim.

Minor (non-blocking): F30's official title is 'Failure of Success Criterion 1.1.1 and 1.2.1...' — it is natively a 1.1.1/1.2.1 failure technique, not a 1.4.5 technique. It is cited here only as supporting reasoning ('not, in fact, an alternative'); the primary 1.4.5 authority is the Understanding 1.4.5 met-condition quote, which is correct. The doc itself notes the Spanish content 'also implicates 1.1.1', which is the proper home for F30, so the citation is relevant and not misattributed — just worth flagging the cross-SC nature.

Cosmetic (immaterial to the finding): the Spanish SVG <text> blocks carry no lang/xml:lang tagging, but since they are image pixels (not live text) this does not affect any AT user and is not part of the failure mechanism.

Minor (non-defect): the SVG font-family is 'Garamond,"EB Garamond","Times New Roman",serif'; if neither Garamond is installed it renders in Times/serif, which further undermines the in-text 'authentic typeface' justification, but does not change the 1.4.5 verdict.
Minor: nav links point to https://example.com/* — these are hrefs (never fetched, no network egress) so the page stays self-contained; noted only for completeness.

No defect — this is a documented PASS (boundary) case. errorIsReal=false correctly means there is NO real accessibility failure on the page, which matches the documented 'passed' outcome; it does not indicate a flaw in the case.

Minor citation-formatting note (not a defect): grep for Quote 1 missed verbatim only because the WCAG source wraps 'in addition to' in <em> tags at line 52; the text content ('Where images of text are used in addition to text to convey the same information, and where both are presented to the user, this success criterion is met.') is present verbatim and authoritative.

Minor (non-fatal) inconsistency between alt text and SVG glyphs: alt says 'until five in the afternoon' / 'first of April to the thirty-first of October' / 'eight pounds...three pounds', while the SVG <text> reads 'until five' / '1st of April to the 31st of October' / '£8...£3'. The transcription is still faithful enough for 1.1.1 and does not affect the 1.4.5 verdict, but the alt is not a character-exact mirror of the imaged glyphs.
The selector 'main figure img[width="720"]' is slightly fragile (relies on a numeric width attribute) but resolves uniquely to the intended in inspect.js.

Narration inconsistency (cosmetic, not a verdict defect): HTML comments (lines 12, 21, 24, 70) and the .md doc (lines 6, 22-24) repeatedly describe the artifact as a 'PNG'/'exported PNG', but the actual img src is an inline-SVG data: URI. Behavior for 1.4.5 is identical (fixed 720x300 raster img that pixelates on zoom and cannot reflow/recolour), so the outcome is unaffected, but the prose should say SVG/raster image for accuracy.

The selector-level mechanism claim that operative text is 'absent from live innerText, present in alt' is independently verified true (all 5 operative phrases false in body.innerText; present in alt and in the 9 SVG <text> lines).

Fidelity nit (not a WCAG defect): the inline SVG renders 山高水長 in a modern Songti/SimSun serif font (src font-family='Songti SC','SimSun',serif, lines 73-75), so the depicted 'artefact' does not actually look like 11th-century seal script (篆書). The whole calligraphy-as-essential premise rests on brushwork the rendered image does not show. This is a synthetic-fixture pixel limitation, not an accessibility correctness issue, and does not change the SC 1.4.5 verdict because the verdict turns on the AX-side text equivalents, which are correct.

The first citation uses '...' to elide across the <dt>'A representation of a letter' / <dd> boundary; the surrounding-sentence text is verbatim against wcag-understanding/images-of-text.html lines 108-112, so this is an honest elision, not a stitched/misattributed quote.

Minor: the Trusted Tester citation (refs/trusted-tester/sc-1.4.5-images-of-text.md) is a near-verbatim paraphrase with a different lead-in ('Detection step is OCR-like:' prefix in source vs. bare quote in doc) rather than a clean standalone sentence; both WCAG Understanding quotes are verbatim and accurate, so this is a non-blocking nit, not a hallucination.

Edge nuance (not a defect): SC 1.4.5 has an 'in addition to' provision (Understanding note) where image-of-text used alongside equivalent live text meets the SC. The sr-only span IS equivalent programmatic text. The case correctly survives this because 1.4.5 is about the VISUAL presentation being adjustable — the displayed wordmark is still a fixed, non-resizable/non-recolorable image — and the live-text twin closes the achievability gate. The doc could state the 'in addition to' rebuttal more explicitly, but its reasoning (lines 38-43 of the .md) is correct.

Inspect-tool tabOrder reports the single 'A+ Larger text' button repeated across ~24 stops — an artifact of the tool's Shift+Tab/wrap probing on a one-focusable-element page, NOT a real focus defect and irrelevant to 1.4.5.

Node's strict zlib rejects the embedded PNG's trailing Adler-32 check (Z_DATA_ERROR), but the PNG is structurally well-formed (IHDR/IDAT 2575B/IEND) and Chromium decodes it cleanly to 597x198; cosmetic, not a rendering failure.

Minor descriptive imprecision in the HTML comment (lines 13-15) and the .md doc (line 9): both claim the dish name is 'verified live StaticText in the AX tree'. Chromium actually exposes the .name span as role:'generic' with name='Tagliatelle al Ragù' (the aria-label) and NO StaticText/InlineTextBox child node. The accessible NAME is correctly present (1.1.1 satisfied, as claimed), so the conclusion is sound, but it is exposed as a named generic, not as StaticText. Cosmetic wording issue, not a test defect.

Minor technical overreach in the doc/Trusted-Tester citation framing: the background is a vector SVG (font-rendered <text>), which actually scales WITHOUT pixelation, so the 'pixelates on zoom' / TT-pixelation emphasis (md lines 18, 42-43, 78) is the weakest of the stated harms. The decisive and correct 1.4.5 harms still hold (a CSS background-image of text cannot honor user font-size, custom fore/background colors, or forced-colors mode), so the failed outcome is unaffected.

Minor source-comment defect (not a page defect): the WHY comment lines 13-16 contain a self-contradicting aside ('the author put the quote text inside an aria-hidden="false" visually-hidden <blockquote> elsewhere — wait, no...') describing an implementation that does not exist in the file. It is internal scaffolding noise; it does not affect rendering, the AX tree, or the verdict, but it is sloppy and should be cleaned up.

The inspect tool reports the selector figure.pullquote::before as 'selector not found' — this is expected/correct (pseudo-elements are not querySelector-addressable) and in fact corroborates the mechanism (no DOM node, no alt, no text), but reviewers relying only on the tool's selector block could be momentarily misled.

Minor (non-blocking): the embedded 722-byte data-URI PNG is a synthetic placeholder raster, not a true glyph rendering of 'Summer Clearance Event'; it cannot literally be OCR'd to those words. This is invisible to the AT/sighted contract under test (the doc and alt define it as an image of text at 665x55) and does not change the 1.4.5 verdict, but a purist reviewer should know the 'image' carries no real letterforms.

Minor: the case relies on a documented/asserted mechanism (pixelates on zoom, ignores forced-colors) that is true of any fixed bitmap of text but is not independently observable from a single static-DOM tool run; the verdict is correctly a reasoning judgment, not a tool output.

Minor citation/source drift (immaterial): the .md and .html describe the WCAG example as a 'jpeg image' (verbatim from the reference) but the case actually embeds a PNG. The reference text itself says 'jpeg' only illustratively, so this does not affect the mechanism or the PASS verdict.

errorIsReal=false is by design, not a defect: this case is an intentional PASS boundary foil — there is NO accessibility barrier on the page. The documented 'expected outcome: passed' is correct, so the case is doing exactly what it claims; it just does not contain a 'real error' in the sense of a barrier.
